Columbia University student Ellie Aghayeva was released on Thursday, hours
after being detained by federal immigration agents who, according to the
school's president, lied their way into a university-owned residence to detain
the student.

Aghayeva, a neuroscience and political science student, confirmed her release
in an Instagram story, saying "I am so grateful for everyone of you. I just
got out a little while ago," she wrote. "I am safe and okay."

The news came not long after New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani
[tweeted](https://x.com/nycmayor/status/2027115998944305457?s=46&t=F-u914q8nK6dJmjHHvnlIw)
that in a call with Donald Trump, the president said Aghayeva would be
released imminently. Mamdani and Trump met earlier Thursday.

The news of Aghayeva's arrest on Thursday morning was first reported by
Columbia President Claire Shipman, who said Department of Homeland Security
agents lied, saying they were looking for a missing person, before entering a
Columbia University residence to detain the student.

"Our understanding at this time is that the federal agents made
misrepresentations to gain entry to the building to search for a 'missing
person,'" Shipman wrote in an email to students Thursday morning.

The arrest marked the first time in almost a year that DHS took a Columbia
student from a university-owned residence. The last time was when it detained
pro-Palestine campus protest leader [Mahmoud
Khalil](https://zeteo.com/p/mahmoud-khalil-prem-thakker-ice-trump-detention-
gaza-genocide).

Shipman had said that the school was working to provide legal support to the
student. She reiterated that "all law enforcement agents must have a judicial
warrant or judicial subpoena to access non-public areas of the University,"
and that an administrative warrant is not sufficient.

The school did not provide further comment beyond her
[statement](https://president.columbia.edu/news/important-update-columbia-
university).

Prior to Mamdani's announcement, DHS officials -- who have repeatedly been
found to have been lying over the past year -- told **Zeteo** agents arrested
her because her student visa terminated in 2016 for failing to attend classes.
The officials said the building manager and her roommate let officers into the
apartment.  
  
DHS officials also claimed Homeland Security investigators verbally identified
themselves and visibly wore badges around their necks. "They did NOT and would
not identify themselves as NYPD," an official claimed in a statement to
**Zeteo**.

That contradicts what Shipman said in her Thursday morning email to students.

"Columbia University's administration bears a profound responsibility for
failing to protect its own students," Mohsen Mahdawi, a Columbia student and
green card holder who was detained by federal immigration agents at a
citizenship interview last April before being later released, told **Zeteo.**  
  
"When ICE targeted students and raided Columbia residential housing, the
administration chose silence over action and did not file suit against the
government to defend the students," Mahdawi added. "Columbia is an institution
that has betrayed its commitment to academic freedom and human rights.
Inaction in such moments is not neutrality. It is abandonment."

The arrest came as the Student Workers of Columbia-United Auto Workers
continue ongoing bargaining with the university. Their demands include
protection from ICE, which the school has thus far rejected.

"Frankly, given the way that CU staff have facilitated the entry of ICE and
law enforcement into Columbia's residences, I think students and workers would
be safer and find more support off of Columbia's campus than anywhere near
it," said Sohum, a member of the SWC bargaining committee, who prefers to only
go by their first name.

Just on Wednesday, students
[rallied](https://www.columbiaspectator.com/news/2026/02/25/dozens-demand-
protections-for-international-student-workers-at-sundial-protest-amid-stalled-
union-negotiations/) on campus to demand stronger protections for
international students and for the school to declare itself a sanctuary
campus.

Hours later, DHS agents entered a campus building and took a student.
